schema_scope: JSON Schema subsets describe serializable arguments and successful verb-ledger result projections. Additional properties remain open unless the actual nested input spec is closed. Runtime signature/doc remains authoritative; these schemas are discovery metadata, not dispatch validation.
execution_scope: All Python examples run inside one Houdini exec/inspect request. Live hou.Node values and Python locals are scoped to that request. Persist explicit path strings in __result__ and use those strings in later requests; ledger {node:path} snapshots are observations, not callable Node objects.

verb_help.summary: Read actual callable signatures and brief purpose; detail='full' adds complete documentation, argument/result schemas and examples.

detail.description: Brief returns callable facts and concise purpose. Full adds complete doc and maintained operation_contract; applies to one name or every item in a batch.

doc.description: Concise purpose in brief mode; complete callable documentation in full mode.

full_help.description: Executable full-help query, supplied in brief mode.

examples.title: Inspect a focused group
examples.read_result: items contains actual signatures, return types, execution modes, concise purposes and executable full_help queries. No full schemas are included by default.

examples.title: Read the complete contract for a selected operation
examples.read_result: doc contains the complete callable documentation; operation_contract, where maintained, supplies input/output schemas and executable examples.

notes: List input returns items/count, not a mapping keyed by verb name. Both scalar and list inputs default to brief; use detail='full' when complete documentation or nested input/output shapes are needed.

call_mode=exec means houdini_exec or houdini_job_submit; query_or_exec is also available through houdini_inspect. Python names, live Node objects and local variables do not persist across separate tool calls.

node_info.summary: Read static node type and parameter templates in a real creation network without creating a probe.

parent.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

requested_type.description: The caller's requested family or exact type. type is the actual resolved version used by creation.

examples.title: Discover Box SOP after creating its container
examples.read_result: Read parameters (not parms or setting_cards); operation_parameters, when present, remains unfiltered.

examples.title: Query an existing SOP network
examples.read_result: This query requires example_geo to exist; /obj creates OBJ nodes and cannot supply a Box SOP card.

notes: parm_filter is a literal substring, not regex, glob or a pipe-separated list. Static defaults and menus do not describe shelf initialization or dynamic menus on a live node.
parent must be an existing creation network. Unknown types report nearby visible registered names/labels in that context; suggestions do not substitute for the requested type.

tab_create.summary: Create and initialize one node, then optionally wire inputs and set strict parameters.

parent.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

anyOf.description: Existing node path, absolute or relative to the explicit parent; a live hou.Node is also accepted within the same exec.

examples.title: Use a live Node immediately and return a reusable path
examples.code:
geo = tab_create('/obj', 'geo', name='example_geo')
box = tab_create(geo, 'box', name='box1')
set_parms(box, {'sizex': 2.0})
__result__ = {'geo_path': geo.path(), 'box_path': box.path()}
examples.read_result: Python returns a live hou.Node. The verb ledger projects it as {node: path}; __result__ explicitly returns path strings for a later tool call.

examples.title: Preserve an empty first input
examples.read_result: box1 must already exist inside example_geo. None leaves input 0 empty and wires box1 to input 1.

notes: A successful Python return is a Node, not a dict with ok/created. Do not pass the ledger snapshot {node: path} back as a Node; use its path string.
Input references are resolved relative to parent; cross-network dataflow requires explicit subnet ports or Object Merge. OBJ parenting uses set_object_parent.

build_module.summary: Build a new editable SOP batch with explicit node specs and a nonempty output.

parent.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

examples.title: Build and retain the real output path
examples.read_result: On applied success read created[name] and validation. There is no top-level ok or output in this applied return.

examples.title: Preview without creating nodes
examples.read_result: dry_run returns node_count/output/valid and zero writes; it does not return created/validation or prove VEX/cook/geometry.

notes: nodes entries accept exactly name/type/parms/inputs; no comment, flags or position field. References may name any declared spec or an existing direct child; declaration order does not control wiring.
None retains an input slot. output and required_outputs name newly declared nodes. Empty controls/helpers can be created separately with tab_create; dry-run cannot prove the resulting geometry.

verify_network.summary: Cook a declared SOP scope and report actual output content, errors and warnings.

parent.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

output.description: Existing node path, absolute or relative to the explicit parent; a live hou.Node is also accepted within the same exec.

items.description: Existing node path, absolute or relative to the explicit parent; a live hou.Node is also accepted within the same exec.

examples.title: Verify the explicit output
examples.read_result: Read output, checked_nodes, nonempty, error_nodes and warning_nodes. Paths may be parent-relative.

examples.title: Read a failed checkpoint diagnostically
examples.read_result: require_valid=False returns diagnostic facts, including ok=False; it does not turn errors or an empty output into success.

notes: output must be explicit; omission never selects displayNode. Default scope is direct children, explicit nodes limits it. Cook/content checks do not prove relationships or visual quality.

set_parms.summary: Apply a strict parameter batch to one node, preserving actual errors and restoring snapshotted parameter state on failure.

node.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

values.description: Parameter or tuple names to literal values, numeric expressions, explicit expression/language objects, or supported literal string patches.

examples.title: Use exact parameter names and explicit expressions
examples.read_result: Read set/evaluations. A parameter write does not itself certify downstream geometry; cook or verify that output when needed.

notes: Parameter names and menu set_value come from node_info/list_parms/read_parms. Numeric tuple literals use full components; tuple expressions use individual component names.

strict defaults to True. strict=False allows explicit partial diagnostic success and returns failed; it is not required for ordinary editing. Restoration covers parameter values/expressions/keys, not external callback effects.

connect.summary: Connect exact source/output and destination/input ports in the same dataflow network.

src.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

dst.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

examples.title: Replace one wire without a separate disconnect
examples.read_result: node is the destination; input/source_output report the actual ports and inputs_after shows the current wiring.

notes: output is keyword-only. Port strings are exact port names, not labels. connect replaces the current occupant; OBJ parenting is a separate set_object_parent operation.

network_controls.summary: Declare persistent control entry labels on explicit nodes, or list the same declarations for native navigation. Names and parameter counts do not infer control roles.

examples.title: Declare the actual controller
examples.read_result: controls contains the current declared paths and labels; this does not verify parameter bindings.

examples.title: Read declarations without cooking
examples.read_result: The exec entry's listing branch performs no scene writes or cooking; controls is read from the actual node declarations.

notes: Declarations are presentation metadata stored on the actual nodes. Ownership is still checked for every explicit write; a control role does not grant edit permissions.
Node delivery cards consume these same declarations. No named-path registry or CTRL-name inference is maintained.

present_nodes.summary: Publish explicit node entry cards from the original execution result. Persistent IDs are stored on actual nodes and saved with the HIP; navigation roles do not verify control bindings or geometry.

description.description: A short, explicit description of what the user can edit or do at this entry. This is not a validation certificate.

context.description: Actual Houdini node category at delivery time.

examples.title: Deliver saved control and output entries
examples.code:
entries = present_nodes([{'node':'/obj/asset/CTRL','label':'工程控制','role':'control','description':'调整尺寸和重复数量'}, {'node':'/obj/asset/OUT','label':'模型输出','role':'output'}])
scene_save(expected_path='D:/project/asset.hip')
__result__ = entries
examples.read_result: The successful original result supplies the node cards. Save after declaration to persist newly assigned entry IDs; files remain delivered through DSH present.

notes: Requires a named HIP. Metadata writes use the same ownership boundary as other edits; references never grant geometry mutation permissions.
Reopening the same HIP and renaming a node preserve the reference. Deletion or duplicate IDs are reported; an old path is never used as a fallback.
new_identity=True explicitly changes a copied node's ID and invalidates earlier references to that particular ID.

focus_node.summary: Navigate to a persistent delivered node ID in its expected current HIP through the main-thread queue. No HIP loading/saving or model parameter edits.

examples.title: Locate an explicitly delivered entry
examples.read_result: Use an actual ID from present_nodes. This only changes editor navigation and reveals containing boxes; missing/duplicated IDs or a different HIP are rejected.

notes: The Host's node card click re-reads the original execution fact and current task binding. Browser-supplied paths, UUIDs or Bridge URLs are not accepted as target authority.

network_boxes.summary: Create, update or remove presentation groups without moving or cooking nodes.

parent.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

items.description: Existing node path, absolute or relative to the explicit parent; a live hou.Node is also accepted within the same exec.

examples.title: Apply a simple group directly
examples.read_result: Direct application is supported. Read boxes and created/updated/unchanged; there is no native box_count field.

examples.title: Declare a container before its child
examples.read_result: The preview resolves same-call box names regardless of declaration order; it writes nothing. To pin this preview, pass expected_plan=preview[plan_sha256] on the applying call.

notes: members and boxes may coexist. label defaults to name; role is an optional color hint and is not a fixed enum or leaf/component gate. Containment cycles are rejected.
expected_plan is optional; preview plus hash is useful when a caller chooses to require unchanged presentation state. Grouping reports presentation, not geometry correctness.

cook_node.summary: Evaluate one node and report cook health without treating warnings or Manual mode as success.

node.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

examples.title: Read actual cook health
examples.read_result: path identifies the node. ok covers errors; healthy also requires no warnings. Manual mode reports not_cooked_manual.

notes: timeout_ms is cooperative native interruption, not an immediate kill. A successful cook does not assert nonempty geometry or visual quality.

geo_piece_stats.summary: Observe connected-piece geometry or bounded Polygon surface integrity without modifying the source network.

node.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

examples.title: Observe connected pieces
examples.read_result: Read piece_count and sampled_pieces. Their extents/area are observations, not proof that parts meet each other.

examples.title: Inspect supported Polygon integrity
examples.read_result: Read status, supported/unverified scope and risk_status; planar_face_crossings supplies its own coverage/skipped counts. These are not a product-quality pass.

notes: group/basis require inspect=True; integrity_only also requires inspect=True. Default piece statistics and Polygon inspection return different shapes; unsupported geometry remains unverified.

create_spare_parms.summary: Create editable parameter controls on one node by explicit scalar specs, code references, or the parameter UI layout vocabulary.

node.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

examples.title: Add a scalar control explicitly
examples.read_result: CTRL must exist. Explicit spec returns node/mode/created/leaf_values; it does not return the scanned-reference shape.

notes: Simplified spec supports recursive folders and toggle/int/float/string scalars. Use verb_help('hda_set_interface', detail='full') for the complete layout vocabulary; do not mix layout fields into simplified spec.
layout is exclusive with spec/defaults/update_defaults; dry_run is available in layout mode. update_defaults changes existing spare defaults and preserves current values/keys.

sop_set_output.summary: Set the explicit SOP display/render output for the user and optionally publish a native subnet Output port.

node.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

examples.title: Make the chosen SOP visible
examples.read_result: Read node/source/display/render. A named Null alone is not a public subnet port; an explicit output_index requests that publication.

notes: This changes the user output flag and is separate from offscreen render_view, which uses an explicit target. It does not verify geometry or infer deliverable quality.

render_view.summary: Render an explicit SOP through the Houdini GUI preview service and return real image, framing and pixel observations. Managed checks and delivery images accept an omitted picture or safe basename; custom paths require output_policy='explicit'.

node.description: Existing absolute node path. Within the same exec a live hou.Node is also accepted; JSON node snapshots are not hou.Node objects.

direction.description: World-space target-to-camera direction. Named previews are fixed: iso=[1,0.7,1], front=[0,0.25,1], side=[1,0.25,0], top=[0.001,1,0.001]; front/side include elevation and are not object-relative orthographic axes. Pass a nonzero xyz vector for a specific object axis; orthographic projection alone does not choose that axis.

output_policy.description: managed: temporary visual checks under $HIP/dsh-visual-checks/<run-id>. delivery: requested final image under $HIP/dsh-render, safe basename only, unique filename returned. explicit: caller supplied destination.

examples.title: Produce a managed observation image
examples.read_result: Read output/artifact and errors, framing, check, stale. The returned image is sent through the Host to the model; the model still needs to inspect it.

notes: Requires the GUI preview service; headless renderer checks use render_frame. Managed checks are under $HIP/dsh-visual-checks/<run-id>; delivery images are under $HIP/dsh-render. Both return unique actual paths and reject executable filename expressions; explicit destinations require output_policy=explicit.
A/B observations use the same framing_frame, direction, framing.bounds and framing.depth_bounds. Pixels and file delivery do not certify visual semantics.
最终图片可选delivery：生成时就进入$HIP/dsh-render，读取artifact.actual_path或实际output/path再present；该位置不证明视觉语义或任务完成。不自动搬动已公开文件，清理只针对明确的本任务临时产物。

scene_save.summary: Save the current named HIP and report actual filesystem and dirty-state facts.

examples.title: Save the current named scene
examples.read_result: Read path and bytes; clean_on_disk can be None when GUI dirty state is unavailable. An unnamed scene needs explicit scene_save_as instead.

notes: scene_save does not perform Save As, load or clear. expected_path is optional but, when given, must match the actual current HIP.

viewport_screenshot.summary: Capture the user viewport for diagnosis, or a requested delivery image. This observes the user display state; it does not prove model geometry or semantic quality.

path.description: Omit or pass a safe PNG basename for managed/delivery output; explicit accepts a caller destination. Consume the returned allocated path.

frame.description: Finite frame to capture; null uses the current frame. The original frame is restored.

clean.description: Temporarily hide supported viewport guides and decorations, then restore them.

frame_target.description: Optional node path to frame temporarily; true selects the first displayed OBJ child. Null preserves the current framing. Live hou.Node values are also accepted inside one request.

textures.description: Optional temporary texture display override; null preserves the current setting.

backface_cull.description: Temporarily enable backface culling when true; false preserves the current setting.

output_policy.description: managed defaults to $HIP/dsh-visual-checks/<run-id>. delivery allocates under $HIP/dsh-render. Both require a named HIP and an omitted path or safe basename; explicit uses a caller destination.

examples.title: Capture a requested delivery image
examples.read_result: Read the actual path and artifact before present. fresh and user_state_restored describe capture/recovery; semantic_status remains unverified until the image is actually inspected.

notes: Consume the actual returned path/artifact.actual_path for presentation. Allocation never overwrites an existing image. A dispatched capture whose completion is unknown retains its reservation; do not remove it as ordinary temporary debris.

network_notes.summary: Read or locally maintain named native Sticky Notes. Notes have their own runtime identity/owner; a parent or name does not grant write authority.

name.description: Native ASCII item name. Existing node/box/item name collisions are rejected.

examples.title: Place concise instructions beside a network
examples.code: __result__ = network_notes("/obj/example", [{"name":"start_here", "text":"Start from ARRAY. Replace PATH or SOURCE to change the inputs."}])
examples.read_result: Read actual text, position, size and provenance. Inspect placement when visual clarity matters; notes do not prove functional correctness.

examples.title: Read actual existing notes
examples.read_result: Omitted notes/remove performs no presentation writes; actual runtime mode remains exec.

notes: Only explicit standalone notes are changed. Notes already in Network Boxes are refused before writing because the current Box recovery scope does not include note members; native Houdini itself supports note membership. Names, labels, colors, and an owned parent never establish note ownership.

The same ownership preflight also applies when delete_node would destroy a parent containing notes. Runtime identity is removed on successful deletion and only a causally restored note can recover its prior owner.

cop_layer_stats.summary: Read the explicit native Copernicus ImageLayer in exec; report full-buffer numeric facts and freshness separately from appearance.

node.description: Exact existing Copernicus node path. Live hou.Node is also accepted inside one request.

output.description: Actual source output index or exact name from describe(node).ports.

max_pixels.description: Full buffer pixel limit; does not cap upstream GPU cook allocation.

examples.title: Inspect a bounded scalar calibration layer
examples.code:
g = tab_create('/obj', 'geo', name='cop_stats_example')
c = tab_create(g, 'copnet', name='images')
a = tab_create(c, 'layer', name='source')
set_parms(a, {'setres': 1, 'resx': 32, 'resy': 16, 'f1': 0.25})
__result__ = cop_layer_stats(a, output=0, max_pixels=512)
examples.read_result: Expect resolution [32,16], one channel and mean 0.25. Read status and freshness; these values do not certify visual appearance or external-source freshness.

notes: Must use houdini_exec: cooking and reading native layers are not inspect-only operations.
Supports Float16/Float32 and signed Int8/Int16/Int32 buffers with 1..4 channels. Unsupported storage, empty/oversized output and failed cook reject without implicit conversion or sampling.
A valid all-zero data layer is not an empty image. Use the declared channel/range meaning, not render_check nonblack heuristics.
Sticky upstream Cache yields unverified freshness. Dynamic/external dependencies and GPU allocations remain outside the bounded native dependency observation.

cop_compare_layers.summary: Measure aligned native layer AFTER - BEFORE; optionally test a declared increment without resampling or semantic inference.

before.description: Exact existing Copernicus node path. Live hou.Node is also accepted inside one request.

after.description: Exact existing Copernicus node path. Live hou.Node is also accepted inside one request.

before_output.description: Actual source output index or exact name from describe(node).ports.

after_output.description: Actual source output index or exact name from describe(node).ports.

node.description: Exact existing Copernicus node path. Live hou.Node is also accepted inside one request.

output.description: Actual source output index or exact name from describe(node).ports.

max_pixels.description: Full buffer pixel limit; does not cap upstream GPU cook allocation.

examples.title: Check a declared additive relation
examples.code:
g = tab_create('/obj', 'geo', name='cop_relation_example')
c = tab_create(g, 'copnet', name='images')
a = tab_create(c, 'layer', name='source')
set_parms(a, {'setres': 1, 'resx': 32, 'resy': 16, 'f1': 0.25})
b = tab_create(c, 'layer', name='after')
d = tab_create(c, 'layer', name='increment')
set_parms(b, {'setres': 1, 'resx': 32, 'resy': 16, 'f1': 0.75})
set_parms(d, {'setres': 1, 'resx': 32, 'resy': 16, 'f1': 0.5})
__result__ = cop_compare_layers(a, b, expected_delta={'node': d}, tolerance=1e-6, max_pixels=512)
examples.read_result: Here after-before equals increment, so max_abs_error is zero. This calibrates the formula; it does not prove that an arbitrary artistic operation should be additive.

notes: Must use exec. Without expected_delta returns measurements with status=unverified and ok=null.

Channel count, dimensions, data/display windows, pixel scale/aspect, transforms, projection and frame must align. Nonfinite data rejects; no automatic resizing, color conversion or coordinate mapping.
Sticky Cache cannot certify the relation. The caller names the operands and mathematical role; a successful difference is not a material or visual verdict.

test_cop_controls.summary: Temporarily perturb declared scalar controls, measure their explicit COP output, then restore channels/frame and compare the full native layer fingerprint.

controller.description: Exact current-session control node path, or explicitly authorized existing target.

output.description: Exact existing Copernicus node path. Live hou.Node is also accepted inside one request.

output_port.description: Actual source output index or exact name from describe(node).ports.

max_pixels.description: Full buffer pixel limit; does not cap upstream GPU cook allocation.

allow_foreign.description: One-call explicit user authorization for the specified existing controller; never inferred from paths or selection.

examples.title: Test and restore a real scalar response
examples.code:
g = tab_create('/obj', 'geo', name='cop_control_example')
c = tab_create(g, 'copnet', name='images')
a = tab_create(c, 'layer', name='source')
set_parms(a, {'setres': 1, 'resx': 32, 'resy': 16, 'f1': 0.25})
tests = [{'id': 'gain', 'values': {'f1': 0.5}, 'expectations': [{'metric': 'mean', 'channel': 0, 'delta': [0.249, 0.251], 'range': [0, 1]}]}]
__result__ = test_cop_controls(a, a, tests, output_port=0, max_pixels=512)
examples.read_result: The baseline is 0.25 and the requested value is 0.5. Inspect status, each actual_values/measurement and restored; after the call f1 and the full layer must be back at baseline. A restored failed test remains fail.

notes: Must use exec. Each case needs at least one nonzero expected delta. Invariants can be additional expectations; range checks both baseline and perturbed values.
Only changed scalar numeric components are supported. Menus, buttons, callbacks, multiparms, tuples, sticky Cache, unsupported storage and invalid baseline reject before testing.
mean_abs_change/max_abs_change use a zero baseline. Their nonzero response proves only the declared pixel change, not the intended region, edge or artistic effect.
Normal returns include restored=true even when a declared measurement fails. Restoration failure raises CheckpointError with evidence; do not continue editing.

Restoration covers snapshotted parameters, expressions/keys, frame and full layer fingerprint. External files, arbitrary Python/solver effects and unobserved dynamic dependencies are not transactional.
